description: Technical export documents, the arguments a reader is handed beside them, and the verdict each one owes: three well-formed shapes, the per-item provenance values their material states reduced to the collection arm's own, and one refusal for every fault the format names.

layout.recordDigest: sha256 over 0x00 || p || iat as eight big-endian bytes || the byte length of id as two big-endian bytes || id || the original bytes
layout.itemDigest: sha256 of the exact original bytes, held in the item field d
layout.provenanceRule: the three values are live, captured and fixture, written in the format's strength order, and a collection arm that carries items states the weakest of its items' prov values: a value that is not the reduction, in either direction, is refused under EXPORT_BAD_MANIFEST, so a collection cannot be assembled to claim live while carrying one fixture. Live software never becomes hardware evidence, because a run of live items reduces to live and never to captured, and a captured original can retain valid hardware evidence, because a captured item beside live items keeps the captured value rather than being washed down to live. The member rides on the two arms that carry items and not on the manifest, because the manifest is shared with the void arm, which carries no material and no list: a void arm states no provenance, and the reduction over nothing is refused by design rather than answered with an invented value. The field is separate from execution assurance, from the claim block and from the assessment: what a receipt declares about its own execution, what the writer asserts about provenance and custody in their own words, and whether any legal assessment was made are three other questions, and since no reader recomputes where material came from, the field is one statement a reader checks against the items and never a verdict about their bytes
layout.encodings: documents and byte strings unpadded base64url, digests and fixed widths lowercase hex
layout.anchor: thirty-two zero bytes, which is the head of an empty chain

key.note: test-only, published so a port can produce these signatures itself, and protecting nothing

layout.assembled: every document here is built from encodeExportManifest, exportSigStructure and sealExport. A fault case edits one position of the manifest map and re-seals under the same key, so the only thing wrong with the bytes is the edit; the signature failures either flip a byte of a payload under the signature made for it or read a document under another key.

vectors.name: well-formed-void
vectors.note: An export that carries nothing and says so. The collection is the void arm and states its outcome, so a reader reports the emptiness and is given no items to count and no walk to have completed.

vectors.name: well-formed-plain
vectors.note: One original inside the document, no chain claimed about it and no endpoints stated, which is the shape a contract a customer asked for travels in.

vectors.name: well-formed-anchored
vectors.note: Three receipts chained from an anchor of thirty-two zero bytes to a signed head, read by a reader that pins both endpoints. The walk follows the links, so the order of the array is none of its business.

vectors.name: provenance-fixture-export
vectors.note: An export carrying one original derived from this repository's own fixtures, and stating so in the collection's own field: fixture. This is the fixture-qualified export a reader is meant to see without reading the claim sentence, which is the writer's words and is checked by nothing. The member is a closed vocabulary and the reader holds it to the value its items reduce to, which for a single fixture item is fixture without a choice.

vectors.name: provenance-mixed-reduces-to-the-weakest
vectors.note: A run whose first and third records carry live material and whose middle record carries a capture, sealed with the value its items reduce to: captured. The captured item is not washed down to live by the live items beside it, because the weakest value wins and the captured item is it, and the collection cannot state live for the whole while the middle record carries that capture. What the row publishes is the reduction on this container, one arm under the same rule the pack states.

vectors.name: provenance-stronger-than-the-weakest-item
vectors.note: A collection whose every item is a fixture, sealed with a statement that its material is a live run. The member is a reduction and not a parameter, so the document contradicts itself and a reader refuses it whoever signed it: a stronger value would claim more than the export carries. The writer refuses to seal these bytes, which is why the row is assembled from the pieces and published as the document a port has to answer.
vectors.edited: collection.prov, stated as live where the weakest item is a fixture

vectors.name: provenance-label-outside-the-three
vectors.note: An item carrying a provenance label this version defines no reading for. The vocabulary is closed, and the refusal is the member not being the one this version declares rather than a guess at which of the three the writer meant: a reader that read the value as whichever it resembled would be reporting a provenance no document stated.
vectors.edited: items[0].prov, set to a label outside the three

vectors.name: companion-handed-and-checked
vectors.note: One original travelling beside the document under a name, and the file handed to the reader: the item digest is checked against those bytes and the export passes.

vectors.name: companion-not-handed
vectors.note: The same document read without the file beside it. The item is whole and the document is not at fault: the reader says which name it was not given rather than reporting a set of material it never looked at.

vectors.name: companion-substituted
vectors.note: A companion file handed under the right name whose bytes are not the ones the item digests, which is the swap a handover carried through a folder of loose files meets.

vectors.name: original-bytes-edited
vectors.note: The bytes of one item edited after assembly, with the digest beside them left as it was and the manifest re-sealed so the signature is good. This is the handover that was changed between the deployment and the reading, and it is the item digest that notices.
vectors.edited: the bytes of the inline original of item contract

vectors.name: payload-byte-changed
vectors.note: One byte of a signed manifest flipped after the fact with the old signature left in place. The structure still reads and the signature is what refuses it, which is the order a reader has to keep.
vectors.edited: the sixth byte of the payload, under the signature that was made for it

vectors.name: empty-collection-unstated
vectors.note: The anchored arm with an empty array, which is the shape this format does not allow: emptiness belongs to the void arm, where it is stated. A walk over no items would close vacuously and read as evidence.

vectors.name: unknown-manifest-member
vectors.note: A member the closed manifest does not define. It is refused rather than dropped, because a member a reader ignores is a claim inside the signature that nobody looked at.
vectors.edited: a member named 'retention' added to the manifest

vectors.name: unknown-item-member
vectors.note: The same rule one map down: an item carrying a member the item rule does not name, which is where a second claim about an original would arrive.
vectors.edited: a member named 'label' added to the first item

vectors.name: unknown-assessment-member
vectors.note: And beside the assessment block, whose two members are the whole of what this version states about assessment.
vectors.edited: a member named 'basis' added to the assessment

vectors.name: wrong-content-type
vectors.note: An export manifest inside a receipt envelope. One key signs both containers, and a reader that took this for an export would report a handover as an attestation about one response.

vectors.name: pack-read-as-export
vectors.note: A pack document, signed by the same key and handed to this reader. Its typ is the pack and its manifest names eight members this format does not, so it is refused at the header before one member is read.

vectors.name: manifest-version-unknown
vectors.note: A manifest declaring a version no format has used. The answer is about the reach of the reader and not about the bytes being broken.

vectors.name: assessment-label-of-another-version
vectors.note: An assessment block carrying a label this version defines no reading for. Guessing which statement the writer meant would be this container answering the question it states it did not answer.

vectors.name: collection-arm-unknown
vectors.note: A collection whose label names a shape this version does not define, beside the three it does.

vectors.name: claim-kind-unknown
vectors.note: A claim whose kind is neither provenance nor custody, which are the two labels this version can mean.

vectors.name: claim-after-assembly
vectors.note: A claim stamped after the assembly instant of the document carrying it: two signed members contradicting each other, which is a malformed export and not a deployment that misremembered.
vectors.edited: claim.made to one second after at

vectors.name: companion-name-is-a-path
vectors.note: A companion whose name climbs out of the directory the export arrived in. This reader opens nothing, so the refusal is the format rule about the member rather than a guard of its own.

vectors.name: duplicate-item-id
vectors.note: Two items answering to one name, chained honestly over the records as given so that every link is right: the name sits inside the hash and both spellings of it hash perfectly, so nothing about a link reports the collision, and a refusal that names an item would mean whichever of the two the reader met first.

vectors.name: walk-short-of-head
vectors.note: The middle record of a run lifted out and nothing else touched, so the successor still names the predecessor it had and the head is the one the whole run hashed to. What remains is whole by its own digest and the walk stops at a hole, which is the deletion an endpoint exists to make visible.

vectors.name: walk-forked-at-the-anchor
vectors.note: Two items claiming the anchor as their predecessor, the rest of the run untouched. The walk would take whichever it met first and report the other as missing, so the fork is refused rather than resolved by arrival order.

vectors.name: rechained-to-a-shorter-head
vectors.note: The same omission with the hole closed by re-chaining and the head the writer would have signed for that shorter run. The links are perfect, so what reaches the deletion is the endpoint the reader brought rather than the one the document chose.

vectors.name: hole-closed-without-a-pin
vectors.note: That same shorter run read by a reader that brought no endpoint: every check the container supports passes, and the deletion is invisible. This is the bound section 5.2 states from the other side, and it is published so no port mistakes a closing walk for a complete store.

vectors.name: item-parked-beside-the-run
vectors.note: A record handed over beside a run it is not part of, naming a predecessor nobody here carries. The walk reaches the signed head and never had to visit it, so the count of what the walk reached against the array is the half of the rule with eyes for it.

vectors.name: record-stamp-moved-after-chaining
vectors.note: One item of a signed run restamped after its record was hashed, so the digest the next item names no longer comes out. The original still hashes to its own digest, which is why a reader that checked digests alone would pass it.

vectors.name: endpoint-head-disagrees
vectors.note: A whole, self-consistent run read by a reader coming holding a different head. Nothing about the document is wrong and the two are not the same run, which is the only finding a signed endpoint on its own can support.

vectors.name: endpoint-pinned-on-a-collection-that-claims-none
vectors.note: The same reader and the same pin, against a plain collection. A pin is never left unused: a collection stating no endpoints cannot be the run the reader was told to expect.

vectors.name: wrong-key-offered
vectors.note: The document read against another key: the header kid and the key in the reader hand disagree, which is an answer about configuration and not about tampering.

vectors.name: untagged-envelope
vectors.note: The four elements of a COSE_Sign1 with the tag around them missing, which is the one structural fact a reader cannot recover by being tolerant.

vectors.name: truncated-document
vectors.note: The first forty bytes of a whole document, so the envelope itself does not decode and nothing about a manifest is ever reached.

crossReading.note: Two containers, two contracts, and a reader of one refusing the other is the property that keeps them separate. Each direction is published with the document that arrives and the answer it gets, and neither answer depends on which key signed it.

cases.name: export-as-pack
cases.note: A whole export manifest, projected to JSON as its own twin describes it, given to the pack projection: the pack map is closed at seven members and names none of the three an export states, so a pack reader of any shape refuses it before it looks at an item.

assessment.states: no legal assessment was made of this material

claim.states: copied by hand from one store on one machine

cases.name: pack-as-export
cases.note: A pack document signed by the same key, given to the export reader: the content type answers it before a member of the manifest is read.
